rivers-osm-water-and-mangroves.objectIds: All 540 natural=water area object IDs and 750 wetland=mangrove area object IDs are embedded in the derived GeoJSON metadata.
rivers-osm-water-and-mangroves.processing: In an offline pyosmium area pass, natural=water and waterway=riverbank/dock polygons and wetland=mangrove polygons were selected within bbox 6.65..7.60 E, 4.35..5.35 N. Water polygons were unioned, clipped to pinned Rivers ADM1 and topology-preserving simplified at 0.00005 degrees. The seven opened ADM2 polygons were intersected and differenced against that same water mask at 0.0000001-degree coordinate precision to derive paired water/land surfaces. Mangroves were unioned, clipped to the opened area and simplified at 0.00005 degrees. A four-neighbour A* search on a 0.0003-degree water grid within 7.015..7.105 E, 4.70..4.77 N found the 21-point derived jetty path; line-of-sight reduction accepted only segments inside the same water component with a 0.0000001-degree boarding tolerance. It is not a surveyed channel or official ferry schedule. State-overview water and mangrove display topology are simplified further at generation time; the city water navigation mask remains at 0.000001-degree grid.

limitations: Roads are original schematic travel corridors joining city coordinates, not surveyed highway alignments.
Small islands are simplified; largest polygon retained and minor secondary islands omitted at small map scale.
Shared collinear border segments are noded before canonical chain simplification; input is expected to be valid administrative coverage.
Natural Earth de facto disputed boundaries remain source representations, not a sovereignty endorsement.
Lagos State's local governments are land only: the Lagos Lagoon and the Lekki Lagoon are gaps, not polygons. The lagoon is derived and is accurate to the raster size (about 22 m).

lagos-lagoon.method: Lagos State (ADM1, includes the lagoon) minus the union of the 20 Lagos local governments (ADM2, land only), traced from a 0.0002 degree raster, pieces under 0.5 km2 and land islands under 0.05 km2 dropped, then simplified once with Visvalingam-Whyatt
lagos-lagoon.generator: scripts/geo/build-boundaries.ts (npm run geo:boundaries; Lagos only unless --nigeria is given)

ibadan-play-area.method: The union of 11 named ADM2 local governments: Akinyele, Egbeda, Ibadan North, Ibadan North East, Ibadan North West, Ibadan South East, Ibadan South West, Ido, Lagelu, Oluyole and Ona Ara. The generated Oyo topology retains all 33 ADM2 local governments. Oyo State is selected only after all 37 ADM1 states are built as one shared-arc topology.

lagos-ibadan-rail-route.method: OSM relation 10699301 is simplified with Douglas-Peucker tolerance 0.0005 degrees while retaining source vertices and segment endpoints. The two source components have a recorded 23.4 m gap between nodes 11936864570 and 6287057206; the atlas joins only those recorded endpoints and invents no other bend.

ibadan-roads.method: Overpass interpreter: motorway, trunk and primary ways in the play-area box and named secondary ways in the core, simplified with Douglas-Peucker (0.0008 degrees, 0.0004 in the core) and quantised to 0.0001 degrees; the source sha256 is in the generated file's header.

ogun-roads.method: Overpass interpreter: motorway, trunk and primary ways in the Ogun box and named secondary ways in the four town cores, kept when a vertex lies inside the Ogun State outline, simplified with Douglas-Peucker (0.0008 degrees, 0.0004 in the cores) and quantised to 0.0001 degrees; the source sha256 is in the generated file's header.

ogun-water.method: Overpass interpreter: named river ways (lines) and named closed natural=water ways (rings) in the Ogun box, kept when a vertex lies inside the Ogun State outline, simplified with Douglas-Peucker (0.0003 degrees) and quantised to 0.0001 degrees; the source sha256 is in the generated file's header.

ogun-city-footprints.method: All 20 Ogun ADM2 local governments are retained in one shared-arc topology. Abeokuta selects Abeokuta North, Abeokuta South, Odeda and Obafemi/Owode; Ota selects Ado Odo/Ota; Ijebu-Ode selects Ijebu Ode, Ijebu North East and Odogbolu; Sagamu selects Sagamu, Ikenne and Remo North. The other nine remain visible in the state overview. The Ogun state outline is built with all 37 ADM1 states, then only its exact raw Lagos-shared chain is replaced by the corresponding 430-vertex path from the accepted Lagos topology sha256 e65bb768f638d863576bf64dc800fb4823777def95813e4ed8171678ec7ac1f9. Ado Odo/Ota's exact raw ADM2 chain shared with Lagos LGAs similarly selects and reuses the accepted 147-vertex land path, so the rendered Ota play area has the same edge as adjacent Lagos local-government polygons.
outputs: src/map3d/geo/data/ogun.ts (OGUN_LGAS, OGUN_STATE, city and coming selections)

processing.nigeria-and-lagos-boundaries: scripts/geo/build-boundaries.ts caches the two files in .cache/geo, verifies the sha256 and byte count, builds shared-arc topology so a border two regions share is one arc, simplifies each arc once (Visvalingam-Whyatt, effective area in square map units of the Nigeria frame, 1 unit = 100 m) and quantises it (lagos.ts 0.0002 degrees, nigeria.ts 0.001 degrees). Tolerances are recorded in each data file's header.
processing.oyo-boundaries: All 33 Oyo ADM2 features are built in one shared-arc topology at 0.0002 degrees. The full Oyo State outline is cut from a topology built from all 37 ADM1 features, preserving shared boundary arcs for neighbouring state packs. No inland water is inferred from gaps.
processing.ogun-boundaries: All 20 Ogun ADM2 features use shared arcs at 0.0002 degrees. Non-Lagos state edges come from the all-37-state shared topology. The 430-vertex state chain and 147-vertex Ado Odo/Ota land chain reuse every corresponding accepted Lagos segment exactly; neither is simplified again. No coastal or inland water polygon is inferred from administrative gaps.
